notes: Prior coverage is about 85%, below the 88% Rhan 2 floor: the chapter's planned lexicon is mostly the numerals (13 of 29), which by design recur in counting runs (Modlen's eggs, Mali's coins, the apple-seller's count) and in every price. Reducing them would defeat the target; known-word dialogue was added instead (the walk to town, the stranger, Arth's fib 'Ar… y gwynt').

Numerals 1–10 and ugain all occur ≥ 3 times; each counting run is covered by the numerals diagram (covers_lexeme_ids) so the local-density check treats them as pictured. pum and chwe are licensed as forms of pump / chwech in the delta.

Mutation after numerals is shown with c-initial nouns (un geiniog, dwy geiniog, tri chaws, chwe cheiniog, tair ceiniog) and in Gaf i ddau afal? / Gaf i fochyn bach? (object SM after the inflected verb, Pennod 12–13).
tafarn is not available until Pennod 22, so the inn is 'tŷ'r tafarnwr'.

Codex review 2026-10-12, verdicts on the [?] questions (all accepted, no text change): s040 repeating ceiniog while counting; s037 'Dau wy: un geiniog' and bare 'Tair ceiniog'; s063 'pum ceiniog, dim saith!'; s060 unmutated saith ceiniog (matches Mynediad De); s099 'tŷ'r tafarnwr' as a workable circumlocution (the innkeeper's house, not a synonym of tafarn); s108 bare ugain; s085 'meddai'r fasged'; s020/s021 'Oes, Mam. Caws.'; s046 'Gaf i fochyn bach?' (object SM). Delta genders and plurals confirmed.

Applied from the Codex review (2026-10-12): C.c2 no longer has unmutated 'yn basged Modlen' (now 'Faint o wyau sy gyda Modlen?', avoiding the yn + nasal mutation that is taught only in Pennod 16; the reviewer's 'ym masged Modlen' is equally correct); un + ll-/rh- exception added to nodyn_en and the Treigladau table; A.a10 accepts Gwnes i and the ddoe cue; C.c2 accepts 'Deg o wyau', C.c3 full price sentences. rule_cy 'Un enw ar ôl rhif' (style) rewritten as 'Rhif + afal (dim afalau)' rather than the suggested 'Enw unigol', because unigol is not in the cumulative lexicon. Also (writer's own fix): C.c1 'Pwy sy'n …?' (G24) changed to the whitelisted 'Pwy sy wedi …?'; the wedi recall cue is now '(wedi)' rather than '(nawr: wedi)'.

cover.alt: The town fair on a sunny morning: stalls of cheese, eggs, apples and wool, sheep, pigs and a cow, and Elen, Modlen, Mali and Arth arriving with baskets; a wisp of smoke rises from Mali's basket.
cover.art_brief: A small market town in the valley (timber, wattle and thatch, a little stone church tower behind; valley greens and slate), market day in sunshine. Stalls on trestles: round cheeses, eggs in straw, heaps of red and green apples, piles of white and black wool; hurdle pens with four pigs, four sheep and a big brown-and-white cow; townsfolk in tunics and cloaks buying and selling, a silver penny changing hands. In the foreground arrive Elen (tall, white linen veil, forest-green dress, keys at her belt) carrying a basket of cheeses, Modlen (short, round, rosy, white headscarf, floury apron, wooden spoon) with a basket of eggs, Arth (11, untidy brown hair with cowlick, oversized moss-green tunic) and Mali (12, long dark braid, dark-blue dress) with a covered wicker basket from which a thin wisp of grey smoke rises. In the far background, by a big house with a hanging bush sign (no lettering), a black horse is tied. No text, no numbers.

grammar.rule_cy: Enw (g.): dau, tri, pedwar. Enw (b.): dwy, tair, pedair. Rhif + afal (dim 'afalau'): dau afal, tair ceiniog. Faint yw …? Gaf i …? → Cei. / Na chei.

grammar.nodyn_en: Numbers take a singular noun: dau afal 'two apples'. Two, three and four have feminine forms: dwy, tair, pedair. un softens a feminine noun (un geiniog), but not ll- or rh- (un llaw); dau and dwy soften (dwy geiniog); tri and chwe aspirate c, p, t (tri chaws). Before a noun, pump → pum and chwech → chwe.
